operations.note: No corpus record states a Copilot agent automation, so this family of ten routes (the caller's automations, and per repository the list and create, one by id with its edit and delete, its tasks and a run of it, and the tools and triggers available to the repository's automations) 404 rather than answer a list or an automation the corpus cannot vouch for, and four of the ten are writes besides. Read from the vendor's published OpenAPI document (github/rest-api-description, `agent-automations`) on 2026-10-28. Measured against api.github.com the same day: with no credential all ten answer 401 `Requires authentication`, where `GET /agents/nosuchthing` answers 404 `Not Found`; with a token, `GET /agents/automations` answered 200 `[]`, the repository's list, one by id and the available tools and triggers 404 `not found`, and the tasks of an automation that does not exist 404 with `error_code` `automation_not_found`, the same with no `X-GitHub-Api-Version` and with `2026-03-10`.

No corpus record states a pull request's Agent Merge enrollment, so these three (`GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE` per pull request) 404 rather than answer an invented configuration, and two of the three are writes besides. Read from the vendor's published OpenAPI document (`agent-merge`) on 2026-10-28, whose `PUT` "is only available to users with a Copilot subscription, excluding Copilot Free users". Measured against api.github.com the same day: with no credential all three answer 401 `Requires authentication`; with a token, the `GET` answered 404 with an empty body on an open and a merged pull request of a repository the token can write and on a pull request of one it cannot, with no `X-GitHub-Api-Version` and with `2026-03-10`.

No corpus record states an organization's or repository's workflow-execution policy, so this family of ten routes — list/create at the org and repo level, get/update/delete per policy id — 404 rather than answer an invented enforcement state, and six of the ten are writes besides. Read from the vendor's published OpenAPI document (github/rest-api-description) on 2026-09-16; each `actions-policy` object carries `enforcement`, `conditions` and `rules` describing workflow-execution restriction, an org/repo admin setting rather than corpus content.

No corpus record states a scanning posture, so these four — `GET` and `PATCH`, per organization and per repository — 404 like the rest of the code-scanning family rather than answer an invented `pr_scan`, and both `PATCH`es are writes besides. The vendor marked all four public preview, subject to change, when this was read on 2026-09-10.

operations.detail: the vendor's spec declares no such operation
operations.note: Measured against api.github.com on 2026-09-01: the real API answers 200. GitHub's published OpenAPI declares a `GET` for neither: `contents` without a path (the root listing) is no path item, and `statuses/{sha}` (the legacy per-sha statuses read) carries only `POST` (`repos/create-commit-status`). It describes both in prose: `repos/get-content` ("If you omit the `path` parameter, you will receive the contents of the repository's root directory") and `repos/list-commit-statuses-for-ref` ("This resource is also available via a legacy route: `GET /repos/:owner/:repo/statuses/:ref`").

No corpus record states an issue's artifacts, so these five (list and create per issue, and get, update and delete one by number) 404 rather than answer a list the corpus cannot vouch for, and three of the five are writes besides. Read from the vendor's published OpenAPI document (`issues/list-issue-artifacts` and its four siblings) on 2026-10-28. Measured against api.github.com the same day on public repositories: with a token, the list answered 200 `[]` on an issue and on a pull request with none, 404 `Not Found` for an issue number that does not exist, and the get of artifact 1 404 `Not Found`; with no credential the list and the get answered 404 `Not Found` where the token's list answered 200, and the three writes 401 `Requires authentication`.

No corpus states that one issue relates to another: no field in `backlot/schemas/github.schema.json` links an issue record to a second issue. GitHub's other issue relationships (`dependencies/blocked_by`, `dependencies/blocking`, `sub_issues`, `parent`) are acknowledged gaps in this file as well. GitHub's description, read 2026-09-29, publishes three `relates_to` operations under `issues/issues`: this list, the `POST` that adds a related issue and the `DELETE` on `relates_to/{issue_id}` that removes one. Measured against api.github.com on 2026-09-29 with a token, the list answers 200 `[]` for two issues of a public repository that relate to none.

These four (list and create per advisory, and get and update one by id) sit under a repository security advisory, which no corpus record states and which this server does not serve (`GET /repos/{}/{}/security-advisories/{}` is a gap in this baseline), so they 404 with it; two of the four are writes. Read from the vendor's published OpenAPI document (`security-advisories/list-repository-advisory-comments` and its three siblings) on 2026-10-28. Measured against api.github.com the same day on a published advisory of `psf/requests` (`GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2`): the list answered 200 `[]` with a token and without, the get of comment 1 404 `Not Found` with a token and without, and with no credential the two writes 401 `Requires authentication`.

No corpus states who starred a repository, so the whole stargazer family is a gap — this listing, `/stargazers/count`, `/stargazers/history` and `/subscribers` — and the repo record omits `stargazers_count` rather than inventing one. Serving any one of them commits Backlot to a star count: the history could be emitted from the record's own `created_at` with no schema change, but then this listing owes `[]`, the count owes `0` and the record owes `stargazers_count: 0`. That is a decision about the family, not about one route.

The family is a gap for the reason on `GET /repos/{}/{}/stargazers`; this is the route where a stand-in would break a client rather than merely be absent. Real never answers an empty FIRST page for a repository that exists, because page 1 always carries at least the creation week, so `history[0]["week"]` is safe against real and unsafe against a Backlot that answers `[]`. Measured against api.github.com on 2026-09-04 on repositories with zero stars: one row per calendar week from the creation week to now, every row `total: 0` with `days: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]` — one created that same day answered a single row, one created 2026-05-02 answered 19, its oldest row the Sunday of that week. Past the last page real does answer `[]`, and an unknown repository 404s. GitHub's published spec says the same, capping `per_page` at 30 and paging backward toward the creation week.

Measured against api.github.com on 2026-10-04 with a body of `{}`, on an open pull request in pallets/flask and in a repository a token can write to, with no `X-GitHub-Api-Version` header and with `2022-11-28` and `2026-03-10`: this `POST` answers 404 `Not Found` with that token and without a credential, while the `POST` on `requested_reviewers` on the same pull requests answers 401 `Requires authentication` without a credential and 422 to the token on the repository it can write to.
